title: fix(plugin-auth): warn at boot about each stored SSO provider whose domain list holds an entry that names no domain
body:
Fixes #33313

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:plugin-auth 在 `kernel:ready` 只读扫描一次全部已存储的 `sys_sso_provider`,对 domain 列表里含有「非裸主机名」条目(如 `https://acme.com`)的每个 provider 打一条 warn,写明 provider id 与条目;sso.mdx 补一句如何在启动日志里找到它们。
- 为什么改:注册/编辑早已拒收这类条目,但规则上线前存下的行没有被改写,且被读作「不指向任何域名」——provider 看着配置正常,实际没有任何邮箱落在它已证明的域名上,运维无从察觉。
- 风险与回滚:只读、只打日志,不写任何行;无引擎、对象未注册或读取失败都静默跳过且不抛错。回滚即撤掉 auth-plugin.ts 里新增的那个 hook。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-stored-domain-entries.ts`(读与告警文本);`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` 新增的 `kernel:ready` hook;`sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` 中 `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` 改为复用 `ssoDomainEntriesNotBare` 的那段(拒收行为须保持不变)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/sso-stored-domain-entries.test.ts`,预期 9 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-stored-domain-entries.ts`: `reportSsoProvidersWithNonBareDomainEntries(engine, logger)` reads `provider_id` and `domain` of every stored `sys_sso_provider` once, as the system (`withSystemContext`, the reader `findSsoDomainClaim` uses), and logs ONE `warn` per provider whose `domain` list holds an entry the register / edit refusal refuses, naming the provider id and each such entry, with the fix (send the bare host names as `domain` to `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/update-provider`, then verify the domain again). It writes nothing. No engine, an engine without `find`, an unregistered `sys_sso_provider` or a failed read reports nothing (the failure goes to `debug`) and never throws into boot.
- `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`: the predicate behind `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` is lifted into `ssoDomainEntriesNotBare(domain): string[]` (every refused entry, trimmed, in list order). `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` now names the first of them; its refusal shape and text are unchanged. One predicate serves the refusal and the report, so the report names exactly what register / edit would refuse.
- `auth-plugin.ts`: a `kernel:ready` hook beside the legacy SSO client-secret sweep (the precedent this mirrors: same engine lookup, `objectql` then `data`) runs the report.
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`: the existing stored-entry paragraph (which already states the fix) gains two sentences saying where to find such providers (one boot warning each) and that the warning changes no row.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch.

Level: `warn`, not `error` (AGENTS.md degradation log levels): nothing claims to be persisted that is not; the provider refuses the sign-ins it cannot judge.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-stored-domain-entries.test.ts` (9 cases), module and wiring:

- a provider stored with `https://acme.com` produces exactly one warning naming `acme-okta` and `https://acme.com` (message and meta);
- CONTROL: a provider with only bare entries (`acme.com, sub.acme.com, bücher.de`) produces none, and the control did read the rows;
- mixed lists: only offending providers are named, every offending entry once, bare entries of the same list not named;
- one predicate: for a table of spellings, a warning appears exactly when `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` refuses;
- no stored row changes: zero insert / update / delete calls, the stored rows deep-equal before and after, one read carrying `context.isSystem`;
- no engine / engine without `find` / unregistered object / failed read: resolves `[]`, no throw, no warning;
- through `AuthPlugin.start()` + `kernel:ready`: one warning for the stored `https://acme.com` provider; none for bare entries (CONTROL); boots with no engine.

## Acceptance notes

- The warning is per boot, per provider: a multi-node deployment logs it once on each node. Nothing is recorded, so a corrected provider stops being named on the next boot.
- `check:engine-double-contract` lists the double's `update` / `delete` as `unrecognised` (informational, exit 0); the double holds only `find` and the three write verbs, which exist to prove nothing is written.

Run: `Tests 4 failed | 5 passed (9)`; red are the acme warning, the mixed list, the one-predicate table and the plugin wiring case; the CONTROL and no-engine cases stay green, as they should.
